source.earliest_relevant_work: Reidl and Wahlström, Parameterized Algorithms for Zero Extension and Metric Labelling Problems, arXiv:1802.06026v1 (2018-02-16)
source.verified_source_claim: The abstract states a polynomial exact metric sparsifier of size O(k^(|D|+1)); the source-screen ledger records an explicit question about improving the exponent and whether dependence on |D| is necessary.

precise_falsifiable_question: For the source's exact metric-sparsifier definition for Zero Extension, is a worst-case sparsifier-size exponent growing with the label count s necessary, or can an upper bound k^O(1) with exponent independent of s be proved?
what_remains_uncertain: Whether a matching k^Omega(s) lower bound exists under exactly the source definition.
Whether later work resolves the question using a different sparsifier notion, a restricted metric, or approximation.
Whether a small-instance construction can distinguish a lower-bound mechanism from an artifact of the source's proof.

competing_hypotheses.H1: The s-dependent exponent reflects a genuine worst-case lower-bound phenomenon.
competing_hypotheses.H2: The source upper bound is not tight and an exponent independent of s is possible under the same exact definition.
competing_hypotheses.H3: The apparent gap disappears because later results change the definition or parameter regime rather than resolving the exact question.

minimal_nonexperimental_audit: Forward-citation and theorem-definition audit; compare only exact metric-sparsifier statements with the same k, s/|D|, and preservation guarantee.
minimal_executable_followup: A bounded exact enumeration of tiny terminal/label instances after formalizing the definition, used only to generate or reject candidate lower-bound gadgets; enumeration cannot prove an asymptotic theorem.
objective_endpoints: A source-matched k^Omega(s) lower-bound theorem or independently checkable proof obligation supports H1.
A source-matched k^O(1) upper-bound theorem independent of s supports H2.
Only definition-mismatched later results supports H3 and closes the apparent gap without a claim.

readiness.local_dependencies: Python-only symbolic checks are feasible; asymptotic proof requires mathematical work
readiness.network: not required for the bounded local proof-audit artifact
readiness.estimated_local_runtime: seconds for definition checks and tiny-instance enumeration; proof work is human/mathematical rather than CPU-bound

expected_uncertainty_reduction: High if a later exact-definition theorem is found; otherwise moderate because a clean definition mismatch can prevent wasted experiments.
independent_validation: A second implementation of the exact objective/terminal-preservation definition plus citation-level comparison by an independently checked primary source.
novelty_boundary: This is a candidate question, not evidence of an open problem or a new result. No experiment or forecast score was produced.
